# Earnings press-release tone and post-announcement returns

*Generated by `scripts/run_earnings_study.py` from `web/src/data/earnings-study.json`
(code at commit `a254683`, data downloaded 2026-10-25T21:07:19+00:00). The plan
was fixed before any return was computed: [pre-registration](earnings-tone-preregistration.md).
Real data; research only, not investment advice. Before the full run, the code was
checked end to end on the first 25 firms to catch errors; nothing in the plan changed
after that check.*

## Question

When a large US company publishes its quarterly results, does the *tone* of the press
release, measured against the same company's earlier releases, predict how the stock
does over the following month, after the market's first reaction? If so, investors
under-react to the words; if not, the words are priced within a day or two.

| Step | Count | Note |
|---|---:|---|
| Largest US filers by 2014 public float | 300 | after removing 20 XBRL unit errors |
| Still listed today (SEC ticker) | 239 | acquired and delisted firms drop out here |
| With Yahoo price history | 239 |  |
| Earnings 8-Ks (Item 2.02), 2015-2025 | 12,501 | all selected firms |
| With a press-release exhibit (EX-99) | 12,303 |  |
| At least 100 words and some tone words | 12,136 |  |
| After removing repeat releases | 11,903 |  |
| With tone history (2 earlier releases) and prices, 2016-2025 | 9,746 |  |
| Development sample (2016-2023) | 7,799 |  |
| Holdout (2024-2025) | 1,947 |  |

The universe is chosen from 2014 data, so it does not favour today's survivors. Filer
XBRL contains unit errors that would otherwise top the size ranking, for example
Standard Motor Products, Inc. (907137 bn), Modine Manufacturing Company (550000 bn), NPS PHARMACEUTICALS INC (3543 bn), WGL HOLDINGS INC (2065 bn), zulily, inc. (1595 bn), BIGLARI HOLDINGS INC. (608 bn); 20 such filers were removed by the pre-registered checks.
61 selected firms have no price history today (acquired,
merged, delisted, or renamed under a new CIK), so their releases cannot be studied: price
survivorship re-enters here, and the results describe firms that survived to 2026.

When releases are published (New York time):

| Session | Releases | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| pre-market | 6,521 | 60.7% |
| market hours | 405 | 3.8% |
| after close | 3,807 | 35.5% |
| non-trading day | 2 | 0.0% |

## Method

Tone is the Loughran-McDonald net tone, (positive - negative) / (positive + negative), of
the release text with financial tables removed. **Tone surprise** is tone minus the mean
of the firm's previous four releases. Day 0 is the first close after EDGAR accepted the
filing. Abnormal return is the stock's return minus the CRSP value-weighted market
return. Regressions use two-way clustered standard errors (firm and day); tone surprise is
standardised within each year, so coefficients are per standard deviation. Development
sample: 2016-01-01 to 2023-12-31; holdout: 2024-01-01 to
2025-12-31, run once. Full detail: the pre-registration.

## Results

### H1: tone and the announcement return (days 0 to +1)

| Sample | Events | Coefficient | t-stat | R² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| development | 7,774 | +26.6 bps per s.d. of tone surprise | +4.44 | 0.003 |
| holdout | 1,947 | +29.6 bps per s.d. of tone surprise | +2.13 | 0.002 |

### H2: tone and the drift (days +2 to +21), controlling for the reaction and run-up

| Sample | Events | Coefficient | t-stat | R² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| development | 7,774 | −12.8 bps per s.d. of tone surprise | −1.81 | 0.000 |
| holdout | 1,947 | −18.2 bps per s.d. of tone surprise | −1.20 | 0.001 |

| Third | Events | Reaction, days 0 to +1 (bps) [95% CI] | Drift, days +2 to +21 (bps) [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Most negative third | 3,249 | −34.1 [−53.3, −15.0] | +25.7 [+0.8, +50.5] |
| Middle third | 3,248 | −7.0 [−25.4, +11.4] | +16.9 [−7.1, +40.9] |
| Most positive third | 3,249 | +25.7 [+6.8, +44.7] | +1.5 [−23.3, +26.3] |

## Decision (pre-registered rule)

| Criterion | Met | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Drift coefficient t > 2 in development | no | t = −1.81 |
| Same sign in the holdout | yes | holdout −18.2 bps |
| Development net Sharpe interval excludes zero | yes | [−1.62, −0.27] |

The Sharpe interval excludes zero on the negative side: net of costs the strategy reliably lost money. The rule is reported exactly as written.

**Verdict: the effect is not established in this sample.**

## What was learned

1. **The words carry news.** A one-standard-deviation more positive tone surprise comes with a +26.6 bps higher two-day abnormal return (t = +4.4, development sample; the holdout agrees). Yet tone explains only 0.3% of the variance of the reaction: the numbers in a release matter far more than its words.
2. **No reliable drift.** After controlling for the announcement return and the run-up, tone surprise predicts days +2 to +21 by −12.8 bps per s.d. (t = −1.8), short of the pre-registered t > 2. The point estimate is negative: if anything a partial reversal of the reaction, not an under-reaction. That direction matches work on tone management (Huang, Teoh and Zhang, 2014), where unusually upbeat releases are followed by weaker returns; the 6-factor version gives −16.1 bps (t = −2.1, exploratory). For these large US firms the words appear to be priced within about two days.
3. **Costs decide the trading test.** Before costs the long-short portfolio's development Sharpe is −0.01. Rebalancing about 52 positions every day trades 0.45 of the book a day, roughly 11% a year at 10 bps, which takes it to −0.95. Holding positions without daily rebalancing would trade far less; that design was not pre-registered, so it is left for a new study.
4. **Date-only timing flatters the result.** 33% of releases came after the close but carry that day's date. Trading them at that date's close, before the news was public, gives a development Sharpe of −0.08 against −0.95 with honest timing, a gap of +0.87. Part of it is the honest rule's extra day of waiting; the rest comes from trading before the news was public.
5. **Two word lists agree.** The pipeline's own hand-written lexicon correlates +0.50 with Loughran-McDonald tone, and its tone surprise also relates to the reaction (t = +4.9, exploratory), so the information-content result does not hinge on one dictionary.

## Limitations

- Price history only for firms listed today (61 of the 300 are
  missing), so the sample leans towards survivors.
- No analyst forecasts: the earnings surprise is controlled for only through the
  announcement return.
- The pre-registered portfolio rebalances to equal weights daily, which makes turnover,
  and so costs, high.
- One dictionary-based tone measure for the confirmatory test; dictionaries miss context
  that a transformer model might catch.
- Costs are a flat rate per dollar traded; no market impact or borrow costs.
- Daily closes only: the study cannot see intraday reactions.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run python -m scripts.fetch_earnings_data   # needs ALPHADOTS_SEC_USER_AGENT in .env
uv run python -m scripts.run_earnings_study
```

Downloads are cached in `var/research` (never committed). The analysis code is tested on
synthetic panels with a planted effect and a null (`tests/research/earnings`).
